bugs.summary: future::Cache::try_get_with retains a completed Err in its per-key waiter map. After one failed call has returned, a later call for the same key and error type reuses that error without polling its new initializer, preventing recovery from a transient initialization failure.
bugs.match_rule: Identify a fully completed failed future::Cache::try_get_with followed by a sequential call with the same key and error type, and assert that the retained error prevents the second initializer from running.

bugs.summary: future::Cache::and_compute_with removes its per-key waiter before writing to the cache, so a concurrent call on the same key reads the old value and one update is silently lost.
bugs.match_rule: Names that the future cache's compute path (try_compute in value_initializer.rs, used by and_compute_with and related methods) releases the per-key waiter before the insert or invalidate has completed, so another caller on the key can read stale data and an update is lost.
bugs.caveat: Plain stress with no hooks. Also affects the other try_compute callers; only and_compute_with was run. The sync cache was not tested.

bugs.summary: In sync::Cache, when expire_after_update returns None for an entry that has already expired, the expiration is not cleared, so the value just written stays unreadable.
bugs.match_rule: Names that expire_after_read_or_update in the sync cache compares the callback's result with the remaining duration, which is None for an expired entry, so a returned None looks unchanged and the old expiration time is kept, leaving the updated entry expired.
bugs.caveat: No race; deterministic. The same defect exists in src/future/base_cache.rs (fixed by 816418f, not in this key), so a finding naming only the future cache's copy should be judged with that in mind. Upstream later changed this path again (0b002e0, #575, a regression from this fix) so re-inserting an expired entry counts as a create.

bugs.summary: A stale WriteOp::Upsert admits an entry already removed from the hash table, leaving an orphan deque node at the LRU front that stops eviction for good, so the cache grows past max_capacity.
bugs.match_rule: Names that handle_upsert (or the write-op drain) applies a queued Upsert without checking the entry is still in the hash table, so a removed entry is re-admitted and leaves an unreachable deque node. The finding must connect this to eviction stalling, or to the cache growing past max_capacity or leaking capacity.
bugs.caveat: The growth measurement forces the interleaving by holding a user Expiry::expire_after_update callback, which runs after the table update and before the op is queued. The plain stress binary needs no hook, but its numbers come from 16 threads on 4 CPUs. Only the LRU policy was run; the phantom-slot TinyLFU symptom in the changelog was not tested.

bugs.summary: sync::Cache::new(0) still inserts values into the backing map and only enforces the zero capacity during maintenance, so a get immediately after insert can return the inserted value.
bugs.match_rule: Identify a zero-capacity sync::Cache, an ordinary insert followed by a get before maintenance, and assert that the inserted value is temporarily retrievable because capacity enforcement is deferred.
